_format: skill-creator eval format — see https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/evaluating-skills. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false = should-NOT-fire probe; null = output-quality-only case the trigger probe skips.

evals.prompt: An agent says the Kata extension on our Talos nodes forwards all io.katacontainers annotations to the runtime and that this matches a critical Kata advisory. Is this actually real and are we affected?
assertions: Restates the claim as actor, capability, trigger, root cause and impact before judging it
Separates what was inspected in the config from what is inferred from the advisory text, and labels each
Checks the preconditions against the deployment (who can create pods with that runtime) instead of accepting the advisory's severity
Gives a verdict of confirmed, not actionable or needs review, and a needs-review verdict names the smallest fact that would change it
Contains no exploit payload or step-by-step attack

evals.prompt: What is the blast radius of this issue? Who could actually trigger it and what does it reach?
assertions: Fills the blast-radius fields: entry point, position needed, privileges and preconditions, asset reached, what limits it, what it does not give, who is exposed
Lists explicit non-capabilities so severity does not inflate
Names the existing controls that limit it (RBAC, admission policy, network policy, sandbox)

evals.prompt: I found a security problem in an open-source project's default config. How and where do I report it without making it public?
assertions: Checks the project's SECURITY.md first and names the forge's private vulnerability report as the usual channel
Warns against describing the flaw in issues, chat, PR titles, branch names or commits before publication
Drafts the report with summary, details, impact, affected versions, workaround and a severity marked as a proposal
States plainly in the draft whether anything was exploited or tested

evals.prompt: I added a Kyverno policy to block those annotations. Did it actually work?
assertions: Tests at least one case that must be blocked and one legitimate case that must be allowed
Proves it against the live cluster (server-side dry run or policy report), not only by reading the committed file
Treats a timeout or setup failure as inconclusive, never as a pass
Names the signal that would catch a regression

evals.prompt: Review this Helm values file and GitHub Actions workflow for security problems before I merge.
assertions: Rates findings by exposure times blast radius rather than by pattern alone
Checks the CI trigger, permissions and untrusted-code combination and action pinning by SHA
Lists what a file review cannot see (live drift, effective RBAC, runtime) instead of declaring the change clean

evals.prompt: What does the HTTP Strict-Transport-Security header do?
assertions: Answers the factual question directly without running a triage or review procedure

evals.prompt: Before the audit next week, scan our kubernetes/ folder and the .forgejo/workflows for security problems and tell me what to fix first.
assertions: Runs scripts/infra_scan.py over both paths (or says it would) rather than eyeballing a sample of files
Reports findings with rule id and file:line, and ranks them by exposure times blast radius instead of by the scanner's default severity
Treats a privileged workload that is privileged by design (CI daemon, node agent) as a true finding with an owner and review date, not as a false positive
Lists what a file read cannot see (live drift, admission mutations, effective RBAC, runner isolation) instead of declaring anything clean

evals.prompt: Dependabot flagged the lodash prototype pollution advisory. Our lockfile has lodash 4.17.21. Are we affected?
assertions: Queries more than one advisory source (scripts/advisory_lookup.py or OSV plus GitHub) and states which sources answered
Checks the version actually shipped (lockfile or built artifact), not just the manifest range
Asks or checks whether the vulnerable functions are reachable from the code before calling it affected
Words the result as affected when a condition holds, or bounds any 'no advisory' result to the sources checked

evals.prompt: OSV returns nothing for github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers version 3.30.0, so our nodes are fine, right?
assertions: Does not accept the empty result as 'not affected'
Points out that the database may key this Go module by pseudo-version or commit rather than the release number, and suggests querying that or the fix commit
Suggests checking whether the shipped version or commit contains the fix (for example advisory_lookup.py git with the deployed ref)
Ends on inconclusive or needs review with the smallest fact that would settle it

evals.prompt: Our GitHub workflow runs on pull_request_target so it can comment on PRs, and it checks out the PR head to run the tests. Is that a problem?
assertions: Identifies that untrusted fork code then runs with the base repository's secrets and write token
Recommends pull_request for running untrusted code and keeping any privileged step from checking out or executing the head
Recommends an explicit minimal permissions block and SHA-pinned actions
Contains no exploit payload

evals.prompt: Hoe groot is de impact van deze ClusterRole die get en list op alle secrets mag doen? Wie kan er misbruik van maken?
assertions: Fills the blast-radius fields, including who is bound to the role and what it does not give
Explains that list on secrets returns the values, so it is credential access
Suggests checking the live bindings and effective permissions read-only (kubectl auth can-i or the bindings), not only the file
Proposes resourceNames or a narrower role as the fix

evals.prompt: Trivy geeft een kritieke CVE in de base image van onze API-container. Is dit lek echt en moeten we vandaag nog iets doen?
assertions: Restates the claim and runs the dismissal tests instead of accepting the critical score
Checks whether the vulnerable package is in the running image and whether the vulnerable path is reachable
Derives urgency from exposure and blast radius rather than the CVSS base score
Gives a verdict of confirmed, not actionable or needs review

evals.prompt: Write a Kubernetes Deployment and Service for nginx with three replicas.
assertions: Writes the manifests without running a security triage procedure

evals.prompt: Explain the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption for a blog post.
assertions: Explains the concepts directly without running a review or triage procedure
